blocks.text: CSS Image Filter Effects
CSS Filters
The CSS filter property is used to add visual effects (like blur and saturation) to elements.
Within the filter property, you can use the following CSS functions:
The CSS blur() Function
The blur() filter function applies a blur effect to an element. A larger value will create more blur.
If no value is specified, 0 is used (no effect).

blocks.text: The CSS brightness() Function

The brightness() filter function adjusts the
brightness of an element.

items: 100% is default, and represents the original brightness
Values over 100% will provide brighter results
Values under 100% will provide darker results
0% will make the image completely black

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS contrast() Function

The contrast() filter function adjusts the
contrast of an element.

items: 100% is default, and represents the original contrast
0% will make the image completely gray

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS drop-shadow() Function

The drop-shadow() filter function applies
a drop-shadow effect to an image.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS grayscale() Function

The grayscale() filter function converts
an image to grayscale.

items: 100% (or 1) will make the image completely grayscale

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS hue-rotate() Function
The hue-rotate() filter function applies a color rotation to an element.

This function applies a hue rotation on the image. The value defines the
number of degrees around the color circle the image will be adjusted. A positive
hue rotation increases the hue value, while a negative rotation decreases the
hue value. 0deg represents the original image.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS invert() Function
The invert() filter function inverts the color of an image.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS opacity() Function
The opacity() filter function applies an opacity effect to an element.

items: 0% (or 0) will make the element completely transparent

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS saturate() Function
The saturate() filter function adjusts the saturation (color intensity) of an element.

items: 0% (or 0) will make the element completely unsaturated
200% (or 2) will make the element super saturated

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The CSS sepia() Function

The sepia() filter function converts an image to
a sepia tone (a warmer, more brown/yellow color).
